page: Amazon Web Services m6g.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 CPU model running at 2.5 GHz. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the m6g.4xlarge demonstrates average performance across several multi-threaded and system workloads. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test yielded a score of 24287.64, while the Geekbench multi-core score reached 8494.0, both placing in the middle tier of tested servers. Memory read-only bandwidth is measured at 946.94 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 129.28 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-threaded performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 965.0 and a weak Passmark memory score of 1804.37.

This instance is suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 18.69 GB/sec, and database operations, scoring 10352.18 on Passmark database tests. It also handles multi-threaded decompression and software compilation effectively. Conversely, it is poorly suited for large-scale language model inference, with text generation on a 7B model averaging 10.51 tokens/sec and prompt processing on a 135M model rated as weak. The lack of local storage and hardware acceleration limits its utility for high-performance storage-heavy or GPU-dependent tasks.

The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark results indicate average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 24287.64 and a static web serving throughput of 18.69 GB/sec.
